findings.title: Counterfeit animal statuses
findings.claim: Human release, protection, and inherited animal-status practices are presented as if Allah instituted them, turning customary distinctions into counterfeit divine categories.
findings.mechanism: The four distinct livestock carriers meet the institutional source frame of جعل and the false-attribution relation of يفترون على الله. The supplied wider parallels at 6:136, 6:138, 6:140, 10:59, and 16:116 sharpen the contrast between stated or authorized limits and humanly invented classifications.
findings.reader_payoff: The four names become legible as different operations on animal use and status that are being sacralized, rather than as interchangeable labels.
findings.containment: The four categories remain materially distinct; this does not claim identical practical rules, a single historical custom, or that the ordinary animal names themselves are false.

epistemic.reason: A citable cross-run publication directly states the attribution relation and anchors every retained branch to an exact focus occurrence; the wider connection rows supply corroborating context without deciding the reading.

findings.title: Reason as a tether on attribution
findings.claim: The closing failure to reason can also be read as a failure to restrain the speech that turns human classifications into divine law.
findings.mechanism: The cognition form يَعْقِلُونَ carries both the supplied understanding-and-discernment branch and the exact binding image. The focus's fabricated attribution is the independent contact, while the 10:100 connection supplies a wider parallel between refusal to reason and the resulting disorder.
findings.reader_payoff: The final diagnosis makes unreasoning newly visible as unrestrained attribution: judgment has not been bound to evidence before a rule is attached to Allah.
findings.containment: The tether is an analogical restraint image, not a claim that يَعْقِلُونَ literally means tying a camel here; the cognitive branch remains the focus-local reading, and the finding does not make every error deliberate.

epistemic.reason: The candidate is citable and directly anchored to the focus word, but the tether facet and its wider parallel are a cross-domain inference rather than the sole local gloss.

findings.title: Ancestral storage of a fabricated cut
findings.claim: The fabricated status can persist because an inherited ancestral practice stores the restriction as sufficient authority after the original human cut has been forgotten.
findings.mechanism: The focus's ongoing false-attribution form is contacted by the supplied 5:104 retrospective trigger. The exact physical-cut branch gives that contact a bounded analogical image: a social classification cuts ordinary access and ancestry keeps the cut in circulation.
findings.reader_payoff: A false rule becomes visible as something that can survive through inherited sufficiency, explaining how a fabricated restriction remains socially operative.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory legacy retrospective and uses 5:104 only as the supplied context trigger; it does not claim that every inherited practice is false or that the focus literally narrates social memory.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk support states the retrospective change and names the context, while the social-storage relation remains an attributed analogical inference.

findings.title: Destructive cut in a fabricated taxonomy
findings.claim: The ongoing fabrication can be perceived as a destructive cut that separates ordinary animal use into restricted access categories and then attaches that cut to divine authority.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence of يَفْتَرُونَ meets the exact physical-cut branch, while the supplied wide walk connects the image to the institutional list and the inherited finding at 5:104. The relation is analogical: a social rule cuts availability and its authority is then stitched upward to Allah.
findings.reader_payoff: The lie becomes a visible operation on use and access, so the reader can see what the fabricated classification does to ordinary relations.
findings.containment: The cutting-and-stitching image is analogical and does not replace the focus's false-attribution reading, assert literal cutting, or collapse the different status customs into one rule. The related tether image remains explanatory rather than literal.

epistemic.reason: The wide reader walk explicitly supplies the cutting image and its context relation, but its source is legacy-unbound and the cross-domain mechanism remains exploratory.

findings.title: Counterfeit authorization chain
findings.claim: Later scenes make the focus's false divine attribution legible as a counterfeit authorization chain: divine acts carry permission, speech is bounded by right and command, truth is beneficially judged, and sovereignty remains Allah's.
findings.mechanism: The reconstructed HFT trace links the focus's institutional naming and false attribution to permission-tagged making in 5:110, the speech and right audit in 5:116, commanded content in 5:117, truthful speech in 5:119, and sovereignty in 5:120. The supplied before/after change is from attaching Allah's name to an animal custom to testing whether the claimed institution has permission, rightful speech, and command.
findings.reader_payoff: The accusation becomes a provenance audit: the reader can perceive what authorization would require and why a humanly assembled status system fails that chain.
findings.containment: This is an attributed, analogical contextual reading from a reconstructed legacy HFT trace. It does not claim one historical mechanism, make the later Jesus passage the literal subject of 5:103, or invent glosses for unresolved branches.

epistemic.reason: The trace supplies exact Arabic anchors, source word indices, roles, and before/after readings, but its cross-ayah provenance test is explicitly an attributed analogical inference and seven branch descriptors remain unresolved.
